findings.claim: ADR-0011, README.md and ADR-0013 still describe Codex install/update as a plugin-marketplace flow (`codex plugin marketplace add/upgrade`), but PRD-v2.md E25 (line 179) decides the opposite: Codex installs as a plain `config.toml` MCP entry, explicitly 'not a Codex plugin', because 'plugin spawns in cache dir, no `${VAR}` expansion'. DECISIONS-r3.md Q11 only settles the project-source fallback question, not install mode, so this blocker raised in BOTTLENECKS-r3.md:48 is still unresolved in the docs as they stand now.
findings.evidence: ADR-0011:41 'Codex | `codex plugin marketplace upgrade` (tested live in the distribution spike)'; README.md:52 '`codex plugin marketplace add … --ref release` (tested live)'; ADR-0013:18,39 same; PRD-v2.md:179 'E25 | Codex installs as a plain `config.toml` MCP entry, not a Codex plugin (plugin spawns in cache dir, no `${VAR}` expansion) | #1210, spike S0'; PRD-v2.md:95-96 lists Codex CLI under 'spawn cwd' sources and 'Codex plugin install' separately under 'No automatic source'. DECISIONS-r3.md:17 Q11 text covers only project-source resolution, no install-mode line. tickets/map-I0.md:31 and v2-issue-map.md:40 '#1210 | Codex Windows project dir falls back to plugin cache | ... | D4: one fixed source ... no rollout-mtime heuristic'.
findings.archaeology: INTRODUCED_BY (v1): the plugin marketplace flow was the original v1 Codex distribution path (spike-distribution-verified.md, 'tested live'); #1210 is the Codex/Windows bug that the plugin cache dir path causes (project dir resolves to the plugin's cache folder, not the real workspace), which is why PRD-v2 E25 moved Codex to a plain config.toml entry. ORIGINAL_INTENT (PRD-v2 E25): avoid the plugin cache-dir path entirely so Codex gets per-project `${VAR}` expansion and a stable project root. REGRESSION_RISK: if the release/upgrade docs ship the plugin-marketplace commands while the actual server install is config.toml-based, Codex users either get wrong upgrade instructions or (worse) a plugin install that re-introduces #1210. SAFE_FIX_CONSTRAINTS: pick one install mode for Codex and make it the only one named anywhere (README, ADR-0011, ADR-0013, release smoke job, doctor/upgrade copy); no fallback chain between the two.
findings.fix: Decide Codex install mode once (config.toml entry, per PRD-v2 E25 and the #1210 fix) and update ADR-0011 (release steps + v1 cleanup table), README.md:44-52, and ADR-0013 (marketplace smoke step) to match. If config.toml is final, the Codex 'update' instruction becomes 'edit the pinned ref/commit in config.toml' or similar, not a marketplace command, and the release smoke job must check that path instead of a plugin install.

findings.claim: The annotations gap already flagged as a blocker in the r3 round1 Codex review (out/r3/A/round1/review/agent-codex-cli.json) is still present: PRD-v2.md:120 still gives `readOnlyHint` only to `ctx_search`/`ctx_resume`/`ctx_stats`, with no `destructiveHint`/`openWorldHint` stated for any tool, even though the tool list itself was edited since (now 7 tools in §7, not the old 9). Codex 0.156.1 cancels MCP tool calls whose descriptors lack annotations (#846), so this was not a one-off doc slip; it survived a later edit pass of the same section untouched.
findings.evidence: PRD-v2.md:116-123 (current §7 tool list, 7 tools) vs PRD-v2.md:120 unchanged text '`readOnlyHint: true` on `ctx_search`, `ctx_resume`, `ctx_stats`'; PRD-v2.md:164 'E10 | readOnlyHint on search/resume/stats only | #1048'. v1 git show ff5b0cff 'fix(codex): MCP sentinel namespace + PreToolUse rewrites + tool annotations (#844 #845 #846) (#851)': 'Codex cancels unannotated tool calls before execution ("user cancelled MCP tool call")'.
findings.fix: Carry over the r3 fix verbatim since it was never applied: give every tool (`ctx_execute`, `ctx_batch`, `ctx_index`, `ctx_search`, `ctx_resume`, `ctx_stats`, `ctx_purge`, plus the doctor/upgrade/stats user-command tools) explicit `readOnlyHint`/`destructiveHint`/`openWorldHint`, and add a GP test that reads the registered descriptors (not the prose) so a future edit of §7 cannot silently drop annotations again.

covered: Codex install/update flow (plugin marketplace vs config.toml) cross-checked against PRD-v2 E25 and #1210
MCP tool annotations / #846 status re-checked against current PRD-v2 §7 after doc edits
Q11 (DECISIONS-r3) scope-checked: confirmed it covers project-source resolution only, not install mode
ADR-0016 subagent case re-read: no change since r3, no new finding
